NAME: Customer Master Merge
DESC:
Your team builds a customer master table from two feeds. The CRM feed and the web sign-up feed were designed by different teams: their columns are not in the same order, and each feed has a column the other one does not have. Both feeds send a new row every time a customer record changes, and re-ingestion sometimes produces fully duplicated rows.

Implement solve so that it returns one row per customer with the latest known version of the record.

Input

crm_df

column type description
customer_id string may contain spaces and mixed case; may be null or empty
full_name string may be null
email string free text; may be null
updated_at string format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss, never null

web_df

column type description
updated_at string format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss, never null
customer_id string may contain spaces and mixed case; may be null or empty
email string free text; may be null
phone string may be null

Rules

  1. Combine all rows of both feeds. A column that exists in only one feed is null for the rows coming from the other feed.
  2. Every row gets a source column: "crm" for rows of crm_df, "web" for rows of web_df.
  3. customer_id is normalized by trimming spaces and converting to uppercase. Rows whose normalized customer_id is null or empty are dropped.
  4. email is normalized by trimming spaces and converting to lowercase (null stays null).
  5. For each customer_id, keep only the row with the greatest updated_at. If a CRM row and a web row share the greatest updated_at, the CRM row wins. Rows of the same feed with the same customer_id and the same updated_at are identical copies.
  6. All other columns are returned exactly as they are in the kept row (no merging of values across rows).

Output

A DataFrame with exactly these columns, in this order:

column type
customer_id string
full_name string
email string
phone string
source string
updated_at string

Rows are sorted by customer_id ascending.

Example

crm_df

customer_id full_name email updated_at
" c1 " Amina Alaoui "Amina@Mail.com " 2024-03-01 10:00:00
"C2" Youssef Bennani youssef@mail.com 2024-03-02 09:00:00
"C3" Salma Kettani null 2024-03-01 08:00:00

web_df

updated_at customer_id email phone
2024-03-05 12:00:00 "C1" " amina.new@mail.com" +212600000001
2024-03-02 09:00:00 "c2" YOUSSEF@web.com +212600000002
2024-03-03 10:00:00 "C4" omar@mail.com null
2024-03-04 10:00:00 null ghost@mail.com +212600000009

Expected output

customer_id full_name email phone source updated_at
C1 null amina.new@mail.com +212600000001 web 2024-03-05 12:00:00
C2 Youssef Bennani youssef@mail.com null crm 2024-03-02 09:00:00
C3 Salma Kettani null null crm 2024-03-01 08:00:00
C4 null omar@mail.com null web 2024-03-03 10:00:00

Function signature

from pyspark.sql import DataFrame

def solve(crm_df: DataFrame, web_df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    ...

Constraints

  • Use the PySpark DataFrame API. Do not convert to pandas and do not call collect() or toPandas() inside solve.
  • Each feed has up to 10^6 rows.
  • Either input DataFrame may be empty. The returned DataFrame may be empty; its columns and types must still match the specification.

SOLUTION:
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame, Window
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(crm_df: DataFrame, web_df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    # 1. Tag de la source, puis union PAR NOM : les colonnes ne sont pas dans le même ordre
    #    et chaque flux a une colonne que l'autre n'a pas (full_name / phone).
    crm = crm_df.withColumn("source", F.lit("crm"))
    web = web_df.withColumn("source", F.lit("web"))
    combined = crm.unionByName(web, allowMissingColumns=True)

    # 2. Normalisation des clés et des emails, rejet des ids vides.
    cleaned = (
        combined
        .withColumn("customer_id", F.upper(F.trim(F.col("customer_id"))))
        .withColumn("email", F.lower(F.trim(F.col("email"))))
        .filter(F.col("customer_id").isNotNull() & (F.col("customer_id") != ""))
    )

    # 3. Une ligne par client : updated_at le plus récent, crm prioritaire en cas d'égalité.
    #    row_number (et pas rank) pour survivre aux doublons exacts.
    w = Window.partitionBy("customer_id").orderBy(
        F.col("updated_at").desc(),
        F.when(F.col("source") == "crm", 0).otherwise(1),
    )
    latest = cleaned.withColumn("rn", F.row_number().over(w)).filter(F.col("rn") == 1)

    return (
        latest
        .select("customer_id", "full_name", "email", "phone", "source", "updated_at")
        .orderBy("customer_id")
    )
